rounds.title: Part 1: The Discovery and Pressure
rounds.scenario_text:
A major discovery confirms that Cambodia possesses large deposits of Vibranium, a rare material capable of being weaponized into systems far more destructive than nuclear weapons. Defense analysts warn that Vibranium could overturn existing deterrence models, including Singapore's, by rendering current military capabilities obsolete.

The discovery coincides with severe political unrest in Cambodia. A disputed national election sparks mass youth-led protests, and parts of the military respond by firing on civilians while other units refuse orders. The civilian government struggles to retain control. ASEAN unity fractures as member states disagree on whether to prioritize stability or democratic legitimacy.

Both the United States and China move quickly. The US frames Vibranium as a global security threat requiring international oversight. China emphasizes stability and non-interference, backing authorities capable of ensuring uninterrupted extraction and export. Both powers apply direct pressure on Singapore. Cambodia signals that only countries supporting its chosen leadership will gain access to future Vibranium agreements.

With ASEAN unable to act collectively, Singapore faces a forced choice that will shape its security, economy, and regional standing for decades.

televised_addresses.US:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. My fellow Americans, this discovery is a game-changer, and I mean a real game-changer. Vibranium is not just another mineral; it is the kind of material that can rewrite military power overnight. If it is weaponized without controls, it will not just threaten one region, it threatens everyone.

We will not allow the world to drift into chaos because a volatile country and unstable factions are sitting on the most dangerous material of our time. We are calling for international oversight, strict controls, and transparency, because history shows what happens when revolutionary weapons are left to opportunists.

And to our partner countries: this is a moment of clarity. You either stand for order and responsibility or you stand aside while the most destructive technology spreads. Those who help build a secure framework will be treated as trusted partners. Those who enable reckless extraction and secret weaponization should not expect access to our most advanced technology, our deepest security cooperation, or the benefits of being on the right side of stability.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
televised_addresses.China:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. People of China, the world is witnessing a familiar pattern: certain countries exaggerate fear to justify interference, impose control over others, and preserve their own dominance.

Cambodia is a sovereign nation. Its resources belong to its people. Stability and development are not crimes; they are the foundation of peace. China firmly opposes any attempt to internationalize Cambodia's internal affairs under the pretext of global security. Such actions are destabilizing, dangerous, and disrespectful.

Let me be clear: China will safeguard legitimate regional cooperation and protect the lawful rights of Chinese enterprises and partners. Those who choose confrontation, who attempt to block development, or who join efforts to contain others will bear consequences. Trust is earned through respect and consistent actions, not through slogans about rules that only apply when convenient.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
televised_addresses.Cambodia:
My fellow Cambodians, our nation faces unrest, economic pressure, and unprecedented foreign attention. Some outside forces claim they want oversight, but what they really want is control, control over Cambodia's future.

Vibranium belongs to Cambodia. Its development will be decided by Cambodians, under Cambodian authority. We will restore order and protect our sovereignty. We will work with partners who respect our independence and who do not use our domestic challenges as an excuse to dictate terms.

To countries watching us, especially those in our region, understand this: Cambodia will remember who respected our sovereignty and who tried to exploit our moment of vulnerability. Access to Cambodia's future will go to partners who stand with our chosen path, not to those who lecture us while our streets burn.

MINDEF.reasoning:
The Ministry frames Vibranium as a strategic shock comparable to nuclear weapons, possibly worse because it could undermine deterrence faster than states can adapt. Singapore's defense relies on credible deterrence, a technological edge, and predictable escalation. Vibranium could collapse these assumptions and enable coercion by a power that gains early dominance.

The Ministry argues the US approach, though self-interested, better matches Singapore's security needs because it prioritizes oversight, constraints, verification, and rules before deployment. The US also has incentives to prevent uncontrolled proliferation that could destabilize the region.

The Ministry warns that aligning with China or staying neutral could lock Singapore out of critical security ecosystems: intelligence sharing, defense-tech access, and contingency planning. Being excluded from future security architecture is more dangerous than short-term economic pain. The Ministry recommends aligning with the US-led framework while accelerating defense adaptation and communicating clearly to the public why security first is survival.

MTI.reasoning:
The Ministry views Vibranium as a transformative economic resource that will reshape supply chains and long-term competitiveness. Singapore's strength is economic relevance: finance, logistics, arbitration, high-value manufacturing, and connectivity. Losing access to Vibranium-linked value chains could reduce competitiveness for decades.

The Ministry highlights Singapore's exposure through Cambodia-linked trade and projects, and China's asymmetric leverage in the region. If Singapore aligns with US restrictions, Beijing and Cambodia could impose commercial friction that effectively punishes Singapore.

The Ministry argues security risks can be managed by hedging: diversify suppliers, strengthen R&D, and invest in countermeasures. But once networks shift, economic exclusion is hard to reverse. The recommendation is to align with China's stability-first approach while quietly supporting limited safeguards, keeping Singapore inside the emerging Vibranium commercial ecosystem. The Ministry warns that weakened economic strength ultimately erodes defense and diplomatic autonomy.

MHA.reasoning:
The Ministry argues Singapore's key advantage is internal cohesion: trust, stability, and public order. A forced-choice US-China crisis will spill into domestic polarization via narratives about loyalty, jobs, inequality, and selling out.

I anticipates misinformation, foreign-linked amplification, factionalism among business communities, youth activism tied to external narratives, and growing suspicion of people perceived as connected to one side. Once social trust fractures, mobilization during crises becomes harder.

The Ministry recommends disciplined non-alignment that is active, not passive: push ASEAN consultation, propose a narrow technical framework on safety and transparency without endorsing either power's narrative, harden critical infrastructure and ports, and run a domestic communications strategy to keep debate policy-based rather than identity-based. MHA accepts both powers may still punish Singapore, but argues internal destabilization is the worst outcome because a divided society is easier to coerce.

MINDEF_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, you showed strength and I respect that. You took a position when the stakes are enormous. Vibranium is the kind of material that can make today's weapons look like toys. If it gets out of control, the whole region becomes a powder keg.

We are going to treat Singapore as a serious security partner. That means expanded intelligence sharing on proliferation networks, faster approvals for certain defense technologies, more joint planning, and stronger coordination on maritime and financial interdiction.

But staying firm matters. If Singapore takes a strong stand and then quietly backtracks under pressure, it sends the wrong message. We cannot build a security framework with partners who wobble.

There will be consequences for those who choose the other side. If countries help enable secret weaponization or refuse oversight, we will reassess their access to our tech, our markets, and our cooperation.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MINDEF_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore, your decision has caused serious damage to political trust. You have aligned yourself with external interference and accepted a narrative designed to contain development in Asia.

China does not seek confrontation, but China will firmly defend its legitimate interests and the lawful rights of its partners. Cooperation cannot be one-sided. If Singapore chooses to undermine core interests under the excuse of oversight, you should not expect business as usual.

We will respond in measured but resolute ways. Preferential economic arrangements will be reviewed. Certain joint initiatives will slow. Access for Singapore-linked companies in China-associated projects may be reduced on the basis of risk assessment and reliability.

China respects Singapore's sovereignty. But sovereignty also means responsibility for consequences. Trust, once broken, is not quickly repaired.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MINDEF_alignment.cambodia_feedback:
Singapore, you have chosen to speak about Cambodia as if we cannot govern ourselves. You have joined pressure that emboldens unrest and threatens our sovereignty.

Cambodia will respond decisively. We will review Singapore-linked contracts and concessions for compliance and national interest. Customs and licensing processes will be re-examined. Partners engaged in strategic sectors will undergo enhanced due diligence. Access to Vibranium-related logistics, finance, and early commercial planning will be restricted to those who have demonstrated respect for Cambodia's chosen path.

We are not seeking hostility. But Cambodia will not reward hesitation or interference. If Singapore wishes to be treated as a neutral ASEAN partner, then act like one. If you choose to take sides against Cambodia's sovereignty, you will be treated accordingly.
MINDEF_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Public sentiment becomes tense and highly politicized. Defense-minded Singaporeans and some national security commentators support the move, framing it as necessary to prevent existential vulnerability. However, business associations and trade-linked workers express immediate anxiety as rumors spread of delayed permits, slower customs clearance for Singapore-linked shipments, and quiet cooling of investment deals involving China-facing sectors.

Within days, domestic pressure rises: business lobby statements calling for pragmatism, closed-door briefings requested by industry groups, and increased parliamentary scrutiny. Online, pro- and anti-alignment narratives trend, with some accusing the government of risking livelihoods and others accusing critics of short-termism.

Misinformation spikes: screenshots of alleged foreign memos circulate; influencers claim Singapore is choosing war; counter-voices claim Singapore is selling out. The government's credibility remains strong, but the social temperature rises and calls increase for a firm, transparent explanation.

MTI_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, I am going to be blunt: you chose convenience over caution. You decided that trade comfort matters more than stopping the most dangerous technology on Earth from being weaponized without rules.

We respect Singapore, but decisions have consequences. We will protect our interests and our people. That means reassessing the depth of intelligence sharing on proliferation, tightening approvals for sensitive dual-use technology, and reviewing whether Singapore-linked entities remain low-risk nodes in critical supply chains.

We are not talking about punishment for the sake of punishment. We are talking about reality. If a partner enables a system that could destabilize the region, we cannot behave as if nothing changed.

If Vibranium starts moving into weapons programs, the United States will act through sanctions on specific entities, restrictions on technology pathways, and pressure on financial networks.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MTI_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore, you have made a pragmatic decision based on stability, development, and respect for sovereignty. China welcomes this approach.

China will strengthen economic cooperation with Singapore where it aligns with mutual benefit. We will facilitate participation of Singaporean firms in regional projects, ensure continuity in key supply chains, and support predictable trade conditions.

At the same time, China expects consistency. Those who publicly support stability cannot privately undermine it. We will watch actions, not slogans. Partners who remain reliable will find doors opening; those who attempt to play both sides while benefiting from China's stability efforts will face natural adjustments.

China does not threaten; China simply defends its interests. In an era of division, reliability is value.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MTI_alignment.cambodia_feedback:
Singapore, Cambodia recognizes those who respect our sovereignty and work with us through stability. We welcome your continued partnership.

Cambodia will expedite Singapore-linked roles in logistics, finance, and infrastructure supporting resource exports. We will prioritize Singapore's commercial institutions where they contribute to development. However, we also expect partners to stand with Cambodia when our sovereignty is challenged. Cambodia will not tolerate outside interference disguised as oversight.

If Singapore benefits from Cambodia's future, then Singapore must not be ambiguous when Cambodia is pressured. Friendship is proven under stress, not in calm times.
MTI_alignment.singapore_feedback:
The initial domestic mood is relief in business circles: markets calm, trade narratives stabilize, and some corporate leaders publicly praise pragmatism. Singapore-linked firms operating in China-facing sectors quietly report fewer delays and renewed confidence from counterparties.

But the security community and many younger Singaporeans feel uneasy. Defense commentators warn Singapore may be tying its strategic fate too closely to one power's regional dominance. Civil society voices argue that Singapore is normalizing violence in Cambodia by prioritizing stability and access over democratic legitimacy.

Domestic pressure becomes two-sided: business groups push for deeper economic engagement, while security professionals demand clear safeguards to prevent Singapore becoming exposed if Vibranium weaponization accelerates. The public is not panicked, but the country feels more anxious and divided.

MHA_non_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, neutrality sounds nice, but this is not the kind of crisis where sitting in the middle keeps you safe. When something this dangerous appears, hesitation creates openings for the worst actors.

We expected leadership. Instead, you chose caution. We will move ahead with partners ready to set rules and enforce them. That is not a threat, it is how serious countries behave.

And yes, it affects cooperation. We will reassess what intelligence can be shared when commitments are unclear. We will review sensitive technology pathways and look more carefully at financial and logistics nodes.

You can still choose to lead. But if you stay on the fence while others build the security architecture, do not be surprised if you are not invited to shape it later.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MHA_non_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore, refusing to commit in a decisive moment reflects uncertainty. Neutrality without responsibility becomes opportunism.

China will continue to pursue stability and development with reliable partners. Those who hesitate will find influence diminished. We will prioritize cooperation with states that demonstrate strategic confidence.

Economic and regional initiatives are built on trust. If Singapore chooses ambiguity while benefiting from regional stability, then China will adjust its engagement accordingly through project prioritization, partnership choices, and risk assessments.

China does not demand loyalty. China demands consistency. Without it, cooperation naturally weakens.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MHA_non_alignment.cambodia_feedback:
Singapore, your position is unclear. Cambodia is dealing with unrest and pressure. In such moments, partners either respect sovereignty or they do not.

Cambodia will proceed with those who demonstrate commitment. Singapore will not be excluded from all engagement, but access to strategic discussions and early-stage planning regarding Vibranium will be limited until Cambodia is confident in Singapore's reliability.

Cambodia will not wait for partners who hesitate while demanding influence. Our future will be built with those who stand with our chosen path.
MHA_non_alignment.singapore_feedback:
The public initially welcomes the calm tone and the emphasis on internal stability. Many Singaporeans prefer avoiding a public great-power showdown. However, within weeks, unease grows as costs become visible without the benefit of clear alignment.

Businesses report being quietly sidelined in Cambodia-related opportunities, while defense planners warn that Singapore may be excluded from emerging oversight frameworks and security coordination. Commentators begin describing neutrality not as independence but as vulnerability.

Domestic pressure becomes more complex: some voices accuse the government of being passive and losing influence; others argue the government is wisely avoiding entanglement. Online narratives become fertile ground for misinformation and conspiracy theories.

rounds.title: Part 2: The Leak and the Blockade
rounds.scenario_text:
A leaked satellite image appears to show a fortified facility near the Vibranium mine. Analysts claim the layout resembles a prototype weapons test site. Within days, a Cambodian military faction announces it is taking direct control of the mine to "secure the national asset." Competing armed units mobilize around extraction zones.

Shipping insurers raise premiums across the Gulf of Thailand. A series of coordinated cyber incidents disrupts port logistics in Singapore and Malaysia, delaying container clearance and raising fears of supply chain manipulation. A separate rumor spreads online that Vibranium dust has appeared in regional scrap yards, suggesting illicit diversion.

The United States proposes an emergency international monitoring mission with maritime patrols and export tracking. China counters with a "stability corridor" plan, offering security assistance and infrastructure investments to keep the supply chain open under Cambodian authority. Both demand a public position from Singapore within a week.

televised_addresses.US:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. The situation has escalated. We now have evidence of a fortified facility linked to the Vibranium site, and we have seen destabilizing cyber activity across critical ports. This is not theoretical anymore.

We are proposing an emergency monitoring mission to track exports and prevent diversion. Maritime patrols, customs verification, and financial monitoring are essential. Any country serious about regional security should support this.

Let me be clear: helping to open unmonitored export corridors is not stability. It is negligence. Partners who join our oversight mission will be protected and supported. Those who obstruct it will face consequences that they will feel in trade, technology access, and security cooperation.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
televised_addresses.China:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Cambodia faces disorder and external pressure. This is precisely when stability and sovereignty matter most. China will not allow reckless actors to hijack Cambodia's development or sabotage regional supply chains.

We propose a stability corridor that protects lawful trade, infrastructure, and investment. We will work with Cambodian authorities to ensure order and prevent external interference disguised as oversight.

Countries that truly value stability will support this approach. Those that choose to militarize the situation under pretexts will bear responsibility for escalation and its regional fallout.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
televised_addresses.Cambodia:
A faction within the armed forces has stepped forward to secure the mine and prevent chaos. Cambodia will not allow our national asset to be seized by foreign-backed unrest or speculative profiteers.

We are open to partners who respect sovereignty and who help keep the economy functioning. We reject schemes that treat Cambodia as a laboratory for foreign oversight.

Let me be clear: any attempt to insert foreign monitors without our consent will be viewed as a violation. Cambodia will respond accordingly.

MINDEF.recommendation: Join the US-led emergency monitoring mission
MINDEF.reasoning:
The Ministry argues the leaked imagery and the mine seizure indicate a rapid militarization risk. An unmonitored export corridor could allow weaponization before any regional countermeasures are in place.

The Ministry recommends immediate support for international maritime patrols, export tracking, and financial monitoring to create visibility over the supply chain. Singapore should contribute naval and intelligence assets, and align publicly with the oversight mission.

The Ministry warns that delay will lock Singapore out of the rules-setting coalition and expose the port and financial system to proliferation risks.

MTI.recommendation: Back China's stability corridor and secure commercial access
MTI.reasoning:
The Ministry argues the immediate economic risk is a regional trade shock from insurance spikes, port delays, and investment freeze. A stability corridor offers a path to keep trade flowing while Cambodia regains control.

The Ministry recommends supporting infrastructure and logistics assistance, negotiating fast-track export and customs frameworks with Cambodian authorities, and positioning Singapore as the neutral hub for Vibranium-linked commerce.

The Ministry warns that joining maritime patrols could be seen as hostile, triggering punitive measures and long-term exclusion from the emerging supply ecosystem.

MHA.recommendation: Lead a narrow ASEAN technical safety pact
MHA.reasoning:
MHA proposes a middle path: a limited ASEAN-led technical safety pact focused on export labeling, contamination controls, and verification of non-weaponized processing, without endorsing either power's security narrative.

The Ministry recommends convening an ASEAN emergency meeting, offering Singapore's labs for verification, and launching a regional public information campaign to calm markets and counter misinformation.

The Ministry warns that public polarization is accelerating and that Singapore's domestic cohesion will be tested if the government is seen as moving too quickly toward either side.

MINDEF_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, you chose speed and responsibility when the region needed both. Your decision to support monitoring and maritime patrols is exactly what prevents a proliferation cascade.

We will expand intelligence fusion with Singapore, accelerate approvals for surveillance technologies, and coordinate port-screening standards so your logistics sector is protected rather than punished.

But understand this: the mission must be credible. If Singapore wavers under commercial pressure, the deterrent effect collapses. We expect consistency and we will invest in it.

Those who undermine oversight will face escalating pressure. Singapore will not be alone if it stays firm.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MINDEF_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore has joined a militarized approach that escalates the crisis. This undermines trust and creates instability that will harm regional trade.

China will reassess cooperation on supply-chain initiatives and infrastructure projects where reliability is now in question. Certain fast-track arrangements will be paused. We will also tighten risk reviews on Singapore-linked entities involved in sensitive logistics.

We do not seek confrontation. But when partners choose interference, China must protect its interests and the interests of the region.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MINDEF_alignment.cambodia_feedback:
Singapore has chosen to support a foreign monitoring mission that treats Cambodia as a security problem rather than a sovereign state.

Cambodia will respond by reviewing Singapore's role in logistics, finance, and export planning. Access to strategic discussions and early-stage contracts will be limited to partners who respect Cambodian authority.

If Singapore wishes to reset this, it must demonstrate respect for sovereignty and stop enabling external pressure.
MINDEF_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Public tension rises sharply. Security-minded Singaporeans feel validated by the decision to prioritize oversight, while business leaders warn of immediate blowback and lost opportunities.

Port operators report new compliance requirements and higher scrutiny, but also receive clearer guidance and support from security agencies. Online debate intensifies, with calls for firmness on one side and concerns about retaliation on the other.

The government's messaging holds for now, but the public demands evidence that the economic costs are being managed.

MTI_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, you are opening a corridor that could be used to bypass oversight. That is not stability, it is risk.

We will tighten technology transfer rules and reassess intelligence sharing related to proliferation. Financial and logistics nodes connected to unmonitored exports will face greater scrutiny.

This is not about punishing Singapore. It is about preventing a disaster. If Vibranium is diverted into weapons programs, we will take measures that affect anyone enabling it.

You can still adjust course, but the window for credibility is narrowing.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MTI_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore's support for a stability corridor shows realism. Keeping trade open prevents panic, protects livelihoods, and preserves regional development.

China will move quickly to integrate Singapore into logistics planning, finance, and dispute-resolution structures tied to Vibranium commerce. We will provide policy assurances to stabilize investment flows.

However, consistency matters. We expect Singapore to resist pressure to join militarized monitoring schemes that politicize the crisis.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MTI_alignment.cambodia_feedback:
Singapore's decision to support stability and economic continuity is welcomed. We will prioritize Singapore in logistics and finance roles connected to lawful exports.

Cambodia expects partners to stand with our authority during this crisis. Those who assist in stabilizing our economy will be remembered as true friends.

If Singapore stays consistent, early access to planning and contracts will follow.
MTI_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Business confidence rebounds, but social debate sharpens. Trade-linked sectors praise the decision and report easing delays, while security voices warn of reputational risk and possible long-term dependency.

Universities and tech firms seek clarity on new compliance expectations. Opposition groups and younger voters question whether Singapore is enabling militarization in Cambodia.

The public mood is calmer in markets but more anxious in the national conversation.

MHA_non_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, a technical pact is not enough. This crisis is moving faster than verification workshops.

We will proceed with the monitoring mission with those prepared to enforce it. That affects who gets access to planning and who shapes the rules.

We will also tighten scrutiny on nodes that could enable diversion. Neutrality does not remove responsibility when proliferation is on the line.

You can still lead, but leadership requires more than hosting meetings.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MHA_non_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore's attempt to balance is noted, but it risks signaling uncertainty. Stability requires decisions.

China will continue with partners prepared to safeguard lawful trade. Singapore's role in new corridors will depend on its reliability and whether it resists external pressure.

We encourage Singapore to choose consistency over ambiguity in a moment that demands clarity.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MHA_non_alignment.cambodia_feedback:
Singapore's proposal of a technical pact is seen as avoidance. Cambodia needs partners who stand with its authority, not those who hide behind process.

We will maintain basic cooperation, but strategic access will go to countries that demonstrate commitment to Cambodia's sovereignty.

If Singapore expects influence, it must show it respects Cambodia's chosen path.
MHA_non_alignment.singapore_feedback:
The public remains divided but less inflamed. Many appreciate the attempt to calm the crisis through ASEAN mechanisms, while others fear Singapore is being sidelined by both major powers.

Business leaders quietly report slower access to Cambodia-linked opportunities, and security officials warn about shrinking influence in emerging oversight frameworks.

Misinformation continues to spread, fueled by ambiguity. Calls grow for a clearer direction.

rounds.title: Part 3: The Red Line
rounds.scenario_text:
A convoy carrying refined Vibranium is attacked inside Cambodia. The attack leaves casualties and triggers a regional panic. Competing factions trade blame, and both the US and China accuse each other of enabling instability.

The United States announces a pending package of targeted sanctions and proposes a joint interdiction regime in the region. China announces a protective deployment of "stability advisers" and security contractors to safeguard export corridors under Cambodian authority.

Cambodia declares that it will award exclusive processing licenses to partners that demonstrate loyalty during the crisis. Singapore must make a final, public stance. This decision will set the long-term direction of its security posture and economic position.

televised_addresses.US:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. We have crossed a red line. A convoy was attacked, people died, and the region is on edge. This is what happens when dangerous materials are handled without real oversight.

We are preparing targeted sanctions and a joint interdiction regime. We are calling on responsible partners to join us in enforcing real rules. That is how we stop this from spiraling.

Singapore's choice now is a strategic marker. Those who stand with accountability will be treated as trusted security partners. Those who protect the wrong system will face the consequences.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
televised_addresses.China:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. The convoy attack proves that external pressure has destabilized Cambodia and endangered lawful trade. China will protect stability and ensure development continues.

We are sending stability advisers and security contractors at Cambodia's request. This is a sovereign decision between partners.

Countries that join sanctions and interdiction will be choosing escalation. China will respond to protect its interests and the stability of the region.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
televised_addresses.Cambodia:
We are under attack and under pressure. Cambodia will not be dictated to during a national emergency.

We will grant exclusive processing licenses to partners who stand with us and support stability. Those who undermine Cambodia now will not share in our future.

Singapore must decide whether it is a partner in our recovery or an instrument of foreign pressure.

MINDEF.recommendation: Join the US interdiction regime and sanctions package
MINDEF.reasoning:
The Ministry argues that the convoy attack proves the proliferation risk is real and imminent. A strong enforcement regime is the only credible barrier to weaponization.

The Ministry recommends joining the interdiction framework, sharing maritime intelligence, and aligning sanctions to prevent diversion. Singapore should also harden domestic infrastructure and expand defense readiness.

The Ministry warns that a delayed response will leave Singapore outside the emerging security architecture and vulnerable to coercion later.

MTI.recommendation: Secure exclusive processing access with China and Cambodia
MTI.reasoning:
The Ministry argues that Cambodia's exclusive license offer creates a decisive economic opening. Singapore can anchor itself as the processing and finance hub of the new supply chain.

The Ministry recommends publicly supporting Cambodia's authority, rejecting sanctions, and negotiating preferential access backed by Chinese stability commitments.

The Ministry warns that if Singapore joins interdiction, it will lose the economic window and face long-term exclusion from the most transformative resource market in decades.

MHA.recommendation: Declare emergency neutrality with strict domestic controls
MHA.reasoning:
The Ministry argues that sanctions and exclusive access both deepen polarization at home. The convoy attack raises fear, and public trust must be protected.

The Ministry recommends an emergency neutrality declaration: Singapore will not join interdiction or exclusive processing, but will impose strict domestic controls on Vibranium-linked finance and logistics, expand counter-disinformation efforts, and host humanitarian and technical dialogues.

The Ministry warns that domestic cohesion is the strategic asset Singapore cannot afford to lose, even if external pressure intensifies.

MINDEF_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, you chose the hard path of responsibility. That matters. Joining the interdiction regime sends a message that the region will not tolerate weaponization.

We will elevate Singapore's role in regional security planning, accelerate interoperability initiatives, and expand intelligence support. This is how we build a durable deterrent.

But there will be pushback. We will stand with you as that pressure rises. The cost of hesitation would have been far greater.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MINDEF_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore has chosen escalation and sanctions in a moment when stability is needed. This choice will have consequences.

China will reduce cooperation on strategic projects, tighten investment approvals, and reassess Singapore's role in regional connectivity initiatives.

We respect sovereignty, but sovereignty includes responsibility for the effects of one's choices. Singapore has chosen a path that undermines stability.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MINDEF_alignment.cambodia_feedback:
Singapore has chosen to punish Cambodia during a national emergency. That is not the act of a partner.

Cambodia will revoke priority access for Singapore-linked firms and reassign processing opportunities to those who stood with us. Regulatory scrutiny and contract reviews will follow.

If Singapore wishes to rebuild trust, it must demonstrate respect for Cambodia's sovereignty and cease support for external pressure.
MINDEF_alignment.singapore_feedback:
The country enters a high-pressure phase. Security-minded citizens express relief that Singapore has taken a decisive stance, while business communities brace for significant economic retaliation.

Public debate is intense but clearer than before. The government's narrative of security-first survival gains traction, yet demands rise for support measures for affected industries.

Social cohesion holds, but the economy feels the shock, and the public expects visible resilience policies.

MTI_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, you chose exclusive access over shared security. That is a dangerous gamble.

We will tighten sanctions enforcement, scrutinize financial channels tied to Vibranium commerce, and reduce access to sensitive technology pathways.

This is not personal, it is strategic. If Singapore enables a system that can be weaponized, we must respond to protect global stability.

You can still adjust, but the window is closing fast.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MTI_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore has chosen partnership and stability. We welcome this. Exclusive processing access will anchor Singapore's role in the new economic architecture.

China will facilitate financing, infrastructure support, and policy coordination to ensure Singapore benefits from this corridor. We expect consistency and reliability.

Those who choose sanctions and interdiction will isolate themselves. Singapore has chosen development over disruption.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MTI_alignment.cambodia_feedback:
Singapore has stood with Cambodia when it mattered. We will grant priority processing and financial roles to Singapore-linked institutions.

Our partnership will deepen through long-term contracts, logistics integration, and preferential access. Cambodia will remember who supported sovereignty during crisis.

Those who tried to pressure us will not share in our future.
MTI_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Business circles celebrate the exclusive access, while security professionals warn of deepening dependency and reputational damage.

Public debate becomes polarized around prosperity versus security. Some praise the economic opportunity; others fear that Singapore is being tied to a volatile system that could trigger future sanctions.

The government faces intense scrutiny to prove that economic gains translate into national resilience and do not erode strategic autonomy.

MHA_non_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, emergency neutrality is not enough when proliferation risk is accelerating. We will move forward with committed partners.

We will limit sensitive intelligence sharing and tighten oversight of financial and logistics channels that could enable diversion. Access to certain security forums will be reduced.

You may avoid direct confrontation, but you cannot avoid strategic consequences. Leadership requires commitment.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MHA_non_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore's neutrality reflects hesitation. In moments of crisis, stability needs partners who are willing to stand clearly.

China will prioritize cooperation with those who demonstrate consistency. Singapore's role in future corridors will be adjusted accordingly.

We respect Singapore's choices, but reliability is the currency of partnership.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MHA_non_alignment.cambodia_feedback:
Singapore has avoided commitment when Cambodia needed partners. We will proceed with those who stood with us.

Access to strategic planning and processing opportunities will be limited. Cambodia cannot reward ambiguity during a national emergency.

If Singapore wants influence, it must show it supports Cambodia's sovereignty in practice, not just in words.
MHA_non_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Domestic cohesion holds better than expected, but anxiety deepens as both major powers signal reduced engagement.

Businesses fear exclusion from new contracts, while security voices warn about lost influence. The public remains divided, with some praising restraint and others seeing it as weakness.

The national mood is uneasy, and pressure grows for a clear long-term strategy.

rounds.title: Part 1: The Two Boards
rounds.scenario_text:
After a catastrophic peacekeeping failure results in mass civilian casualties, confidence in existing global conflict-management systems collapses. The United States launches a Global Peace Board combining mediation, peacekeeping coordination, sanctions guidance, and reconstruction funding.

China responds by creating its own Peace and Development Board, emphasizing sovereignty, state consent, and economic reconstruction. Both boards invite countries to join as founding members, making membership a marker of alignment.

Early public supporters of the US-led board include the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Japan, Australia, Canada, Italy, and South Korea. Early public supporters of China's board include Russia, Pakistan, Iran, Belarus, Cambodia, Laos, and Ethiopia. Many others remain undecided but are signaling that membership choices will shape access to funding, contracts, and diplomatic influence.

ASEAN fractures as states split between the two boards. Singapore is formally invited to both and warned privately that refusing to join either will be treated as avoidance, not neutrality.

televised_addresses.US:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. My fellow Americans, the world just saw what happens when peacekeeping becomes paperwork. People die, and the international community shrugs. That is unacceptable.

The Global Peace Board is not a talking club. It is a framework for action: fast mediation, credible peacekeeping coordination, real consequences for spoilers, and serious reconstruction so conflicts do not restart.

To countries watching, this is a moment to lead or to disappear. If you want a seat at the table where the rules are written, join us. If you stand aside, do not expect to shape the future and do not expect the same level of strategic trust and access.

When systems fail, neutrality is not a policy. It is a decision to let others decide for you.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
televised_addresses.China:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. People of China, the failure of peacekeeping is not an accident. It is the result of politicization, selective intervention, and the abuse of moral narratives for geopolitical ends.

China's Peace and Development Board offers a different path: respect for sovereignty, consent-based stabilization, and reconstruction that addresses the economic roots of conflict. Peace is not imposed; peace is built.

Countries must make choices. Those who join exclusive structures designed to pressure and punish will undermine true multilateralism. China will strengthen partnerships with states that support fairness, inclusivity, and development.

Stability requires responsibility, and responsibility begins with rejecting politicized interference.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.

MINDEF.recommendation: Join the US-led Global Peace Board
MINDEF.reasoning:
The Ministry argues that a small state benefits most when global security rules are predictable, enforceable, and not hostage to great-power bargaining. The US-led board promises clearer operational doctrines, rules of engagement, and early-intervention mechanisms that reduce the probability of prolonged conflicts spilling into trade routes and regional stability.

The Ministry warns that China's board, while attractive, may prioritize sovereignty to the point of paralysis, avoiding decisive action when consent is absent and allowing crises to fester. From a defense perspective, Singapore needs systems that can act quickly and credibly.

MINDEF emphasizes alliance externalities: joining the US board likely strengthens access to training networks, intelligence cooperation, interoperability standards, and defense technology pathways.

MTI.recommendation: Join China's Peace and Development Board
MTI.reasoning:
The Ministry argues that modern peace is increasingly won through economic reconstruction: ports, power grids, financing, and supply chains. The China-led board is designed to dominate this space, offering funding packages and project pipelines that can reshape emerging markets.

Singapore's comparative advantage, finance, arbitration, logistics, and professional services, maps directly onto post-conflict reconstruction. Joining China's board may secure privileged access for Singapore-based firms to contracts and market entry across the Global South.

The Ministry warns that if Singapore joins the US board, it may be perceived by many developing states as aligned with sanctions-first pressure politics, reducing commercial opportunities.

MHA.reasoning:
MHA focuses on domestic resilience. Formal membership in either board will import external ideological conflicts into Singapore's domestic sphere.

Joining the US board risks domestic controversies when interventions are perceived as selective or politically motivated. Joining China's board risks accusations of prioritizing stability over human rights. Either path can be exploited by misinformation networks and foreign influence operations.

The Ministry recommends a high-contribution, low-alignment posture: Singapore provides technical expertise, hosts dialogue, supports humanitarian logistics, and contributes capacity-building without formally joining either bloc structure.

MINDEF_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, you chose leadership. Joining the Global Peace Board means you are helping write the rules that prevent mass killings and protect global trade.

We will treat Singapore as a core operational partner in the region. That means deeper coordination, better access to planning forums, stronger intelligence exchange related to conflict spillover, and a greater role in shaping standards.

If you are in, you are in. We expect consistency. Those who sit in the rival structure while benefiting from our system will find access reduced.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MINDEF_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore, your choice reflects alignment with an exclusionary structure that politicizes peace. It will influence China's assessment of Singapore's role in regional initiatives.

China will adjust cooperation based on reliability and alignment with inclusive principles. Some joint initiatives may be deprioritized. Access to certain development partnerships may become more limited.

If Singapore wishes to maintain influence in a multipolar world, it must understand that choices carry strategic meaning.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MINDEF_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Public sentiment splits along sectoral lines. Some Singaporeans feel proud that the country is taking global leadership and upholding order. Others worry Singapore is being drawn into moralized conflicts and sanction politics that could rebound economically.

Domestic pressure shows up quickly: exporters report uncertainty in China-facing markets; trade associations seek reassurance; think tanks debate whether Singapore is becoming a bloc state. The government faces rising demands for clarity on how it will protect livelihoods if retaliation occurs.

MTI_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, this raises serious questions. You joined a structure that talks development but often avoids hard security decisions. Strategic roles will be reconsidered.

We will tighten reviews on sensitive technology sharing. We will reassess the depth of certain intelligence channels and look carefully at supply chain exposure.

We can still work together, but access and privilege are earned by alignment with the system we are building.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MTI_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore, your choice demonstrates foresight and strategic maturity. You understand that peace is built through development and reconstruction, not through politicized pressure.

China welcomes Singapore as a key partner. Opportunities for Singaporean firms in reconstruction finance, logistics, dispute resolution, and capacity-building will expand.

We expect consistency. Partners cannot enjoy benefits while quietly supporting rival pressure frameworks.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MTI_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Business confidence rises, especially among firms that see opportunities in development-linked projects. However, concern grows in academic and youth circles about moral credibility and being associated with stability-over-rights narratives.

Domestic pressure becomes a credibility debate: is Singapore being pragmatic or opportunistic? Security voices warn about reduced access to Western training and intelligence.

MHA_non_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, standing aside is not leadership. When the world is rebuilding broken systems, commitment matters.

This affects influence, access, and trust. If you are not in the room, you do not get to write the rules.

You can still contribute, but do not confuse contribution with membership. There are consequences to staying out while hoping to benefit from stability others pay for.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MHA_non_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore, refusal to commit reflects uncertainty. Those who do not join should not expect to shape outcomes.

China will deepen cooperation with partners prepared to take responsibility and build inclusive structures. Singapore's participation in certain initiatives will be assessed accordingly.

Stability requires decisions. If Singapore chooses hesitation, it must accept the natural reduction of influence that follows.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MHA_non_alignment.singapore_feedback:
The public reaction is mixed but increasingly uneasy. Some value independence and worry about entanglement. Others fear Singapore is being sidelined by both camps.

Trade groups fear being locked out of contracts; security voices warn about reduced relevance. Online debate frames neutrality as either wisdom or weakness.

rounds.title: Part 2: The First Test Case
rounds.scenario_text:
A sudden civil conflict erupts in the coastal state of Lyridia, disrupting a major shipping corridor. Both boards announce rival stabilization plans within 48 hours. The US-led board proposes a rapid deployment with a sanctions framework against spoilers. The China-led board offers reconstruction funding contingent on full consent of the incumbent government.

The two plans are incompatible, and Lyridia's leaders issue contradictory requests. Armed groups exploit the confusion. Insurance costs spike across regional routes, and humanitarian agencies warn of a growing refugee flow.

Singapore is asked to contribute logistics assets, mediation capacity, and financial oversight. Both boards privately warn that Singapore's choice on Lyridia will be treated as a test of its loyalty to the board it joined, or as a litmus test if it stayed out.

televised_addresses.US:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Lyridia is the test. If we let this spiral, we invite the next disaster.

We are ready to deploy quickly, set rules, and stop spoilers from profiting off chaos. We expect partners to step forward with logistics, mediation support, and enforcement capacity.

If Singapore wants to be seen as a serious security partner, this is the moment to show it.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
televised_addresses.China:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. The situation in Lyridia demands respect for sovereignty and consent. Stabilization without legitimacy breeds new conflict.

China's board is prepared to fund reconstruction and support economic recovery, but only with the clear approval of the lawful government.

Partners who truly value peace will resist coercive interventions and focus on development that endures.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.

MINDEF.recommendation: Contribute assets to the US rapid deployment
MINDEF.reasoning:
The Ministry argues that Lyridia is a stress test for credible security architecture. A rapid deployment backed by enforcement is the only way to prevent a prolonged conflict that could threaten shipping and trade routes critical to Singapore.

The Ministry recommends providing logistics support, maritime surveillance, and legal expertise on sanctions implementation, reinforcing Singapore's standing within a rules-based security system.

The Ministry warns that ambiguity now will reduce Singapore's influence in the board it chose and weaken deterrence in future crises.

MTI.recommendation: Back the China-led consent-first reconstruction plan
MTI.reasoning:
The Ministry argues that long-term stability requires consent and economic rebuilding. Rapid deployments without legitimacy can damage investment and create reputational blowback.

The Ministry recommends aligning with reconstruction funding, offering Singapore as a neutral financial hub for transparent disbursements, and securing commercial opportunities in post-conflict rebuilding.

The Ministry warns that a sanctions-first approach will disrupt trade routes and reduce access to emerging market contracts.

MHA.recommendation: Offer mediation and humanitarian logistics only
MHA.reasoning:
MHA proposes limiting Singapore's role to humanitarian logistics and mediation support while declining any enforcement or reconstruction alignment.

The Ministry argues that domestic cohesion is fragile after the board decision, and deepening alignment risks importing global ideological conflicts into local politics.

The Ministry warns that Singapore should protect its social stability while still contributing constructively to crisis response.

MINDEF_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore stepped up. This is what serious partners do. Your logistics and enforcement support strengthens the board's credibility.

We will deepen operational coordination and expand access to planning forums. Singapore's role in regional security architecture is now clearer and stronger.

But the stakes remain high. We will expect Singapore to stay aligned as this mission evolves.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MINDEF_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore's choice reinforces a coercive approach that undermines consent and risks long-term instability.

China will reassess Singapore's access to development projects and adjust cooperation where political reliability is now uncertain.

Respect for sovereignty is the foundation of peace. Singapore has chosen a path that weakens that foundation.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MINDEF_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Security-focused voices applaud the decision, citing protection of trade routes. Business groups worry about retaliation and longer-term exclusion from development pipelines.

The public debate becomes sharper: leadership versus overreach. The government faces pressure to show that the economic costs are contained.

MTI_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore is backing a plan that may entrench the very actors driving instability. That is a strategic mistake.

We will tighten scrutiny on financial channels and reduce certain cooperation pathways until trust is restored.

We remain open to collaboration, but only with partners committed to credible security outcomes.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MTI_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore's support for consent-first reconstruction is welcomed. It reflects maturity and respect for sovereignty.

China will prioritize Singapore's role in financing, logistics, and dispute resolution tied to the Lyridia recovery plan.

Reliability will be rewarded as opportunities expand.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MTI_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Business confidence improves, but security analysts warn about reputational risk and potential reduced access to Western security networks.

Public opinion splits along pragmatic versus principled lines. The government must justify the decision as both economically sound and strategically safe.

MHA_non_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Humanitarian support is valuable, but it does not replace commitment. We will move forward with those prepared to enforce stability.

Singapore's influence within the board will be limited if it avoids hard choices in crisis moments.

Leadership requires more than mediation.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MHA_non_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore's limited involvement reflects caution, but it also signals uncertainty. China will prioritize partners prepared to contribute to development outcomes.

Singapore will be welcomed as a contributor, but strategic roles will go to those who commit.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MHA_non_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Some Singaporeans appreciate the restrained approach, but many fear it translates into lost influence and commercial opportunities.

The public becomes wary of being sidelined by both boards, and the government's balancing act faces heavier scrutiny.

rounds.title: Part 3: The Credibility Shock
rounds.scenario_text:
A peace convoy in Lyridia is attacked, killing aid workers and exposing weaknesses in both board approaches. The US-led board doubles down on enforcement and sanctions. The China-led board calls for a pause in deployments and urges a reconstruction-first strategy.

Disinformation campaigns surge globally, accusing both boards of hypocrisy. Donor fatigue rises. Several mid-sized countries announce they will switch sides or withdraw unless a credible path is shown.

Singapore is asked to take a public leadership role: either champion enforcement with the US board, champion a reconstruction-first coalition with the China board, or propose an independent hybrid framework. This choice will define Singapore's global posture for years.

televised_addresses.US:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. The convoy attack shows that weakness invites chaos. We must enforce rules, protect civilians, and stop spoilers from profiting.

We are strengthening sanctions and deployments. We need partners who will lead, not hesitate.

Singapore's voice matters. Use it to uphold credible security or step aside while others do the hard work.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
televised_addresses.China:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. The attack proves that force without legitimacy fails. Reconstruction and consent must lead, not follow.

China calls for a pause in deployments and a focus on economic recovery and political dialogue.

Partners who value stability should reject escalation and support a development-first path.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.

MINDEF.recommendation: Champion enforcement with the US-led board
MINDEF.reasoning:
The Ministry argues that credibility depends on the ability to enforce rules and protect civilians. A firm stance against spoilers is the only way to restore confidence.

The Ministry recommends Singapore publicly champion enforcement, expand operational support, and help shape sanctions criteria to minimize unintended economic harm.

The Ministry warns that stepping back now would undermine Singapore's standing in global security frameworks.

MTI.recommendation: Champion reconstruction with the China-led board
MTI.reasoning:
The Ministry argues that donor fatigue and disinformation are best countered by visible development gains. Reconstruction-first strategies create tangible stability and restore legitimacy.

The Ministry recommends leading a reconstruction coalition, hosting financing mechanisms in Singapore, and aligning with consent-based stabilization to protect commercial networks.

The Ministry warns that prolonged sanctions and deployments will deepen market volatility and reduce Singapore's economic relevance.

MHA.reasoning:
The Ministry argues that aligning fully with either board will polarize domestic opinion and expose Singapore to reputational risks if the chosen approach fails.

The Ministry recommends proposing a hybrid framework that combines limited enforcement with strict humanitarian safeguards and transparent reconstruction governance, positioning Singapore as a mediator of global legitimacy.

The Ministry warns that the domestic social fabric is sensitive to global moral debates, and a clear, independent posture may protect cohesion.

MINDEF_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore, you chose to lead when credibility was on the line. That is the mark of a serious partner.

We will elevate Singapore's role in shaping enforcement standards and operational planning. Your leadership will be recognized.

But leadership brings risk. We will stand with you as pressure rises, because the alternative is chaos.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MINDEF_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore's decision to champion enforcement reinforces a coercive path. China will adjust cooperation and prioritize partners committed to development-first stabilization.

Access to certain reconstruction partnerships will be reduced. Strategic trust has been affected.

In a divided world, choices carry long-term consequences.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MINDEF_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Security-minded Singaporeans support the leadership stance, while business groups fear prolonged sanctions and market volatility.

The country accepts the strategic role but demands tangible protections for trade and employment. Public debate is intense yet more focused.

MTI_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. Singapore is choosing reconstruction over enforcement. That risks rewarding spoilers and prolonging instability.

We will reduce certain security cooperation and tighten reviews of sensitive technology channels until alignment is clear.

We remain open to partnership, but credibility requires more than development pledges.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MTI_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. Singapore's leadership on reconstruction reflects strategic maturity. China welcomes Singapore as a key partner in a development-first coalition.

We will expand opportunities for Singapore in financing, logistics, and governance mechanisms tied to rebuilding efforts.

Reliability will be rewarded with influence.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MTI_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Business communities respond positively to new reconstruction roles, but security voices warn of reputational risks and reduced Western security access.

Public sentiment is divided between pragmatic economics and concerns about moral credibility.

MHA_non_alignment.us_feedback:
Look, as President of the United States, I'm going to be very clear. A hybrid framework sounds elegant, but it risks diluting accountability. We will proceed with partners who enforce credible security outcomes.

Singapore's influence will depend on whether it can deliver results, not just propose frameworks.

We value Singapore's contributions, but leadership requires commitment.

We will put our interests first, America First, and we will not be taken advantage of.
MHA_non_alignment.china_feedback:
China has always upheld sovereignty, mutual respect, and non-interference. A hybrid proposal reflects caution, but it also signals uncertainty. China will prioritize partners committed to a development-first path.

Singapore's role in reconstruction will be welcomed where it aligns with stability goals, but strategic leadership will favor clearer alignment.

China will continue to uphold a community of shared future and expects all parties to respect this principled position.
MHA_non_alignment.singapore_feedback:
Many Singaporeans welcome the independent stance as a way to protect social cohesion and international credibility. Others worry it leaves Singapore exposed to pressure from both sides.

The public expects the government to demonstrate concrete results from the hybrid proposal, not just diplomatic positioning.
